name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should add a 2px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px white stroke at 70% opacity to improve keyboard navigation. This decision balances visual clarity with subtle feedback, making it easier for users to track their focus. By choosing a 70% opacity, we're trading off some visual prominence for reduced visual noise, which is a worthwhile trade-off to avoid overwhelming users. This focus ring style is consistent with our previous discussions and will enhance the overall accessibility of EXCAVA.

name: Reader
text: The 2px ring with 70% white stroke fails WCAG 2.2 AA on high-contrast modes—users see a faint or broken ring. A 3px solid #005fcc ring with no white stroke meets AA contrast and stays visible on all devices. Test it in Windows High Contrast Mode and iOS VoiceOver to settle the argument.

name: Ramp
text:
We’ll use a 3px solid #005fcc focus ring with no white stroke. This meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in high-contrast modes and stays visible on all devices, fixing the faint-ring problem. The trade-off is a slightly thicker ring, but it’s the only way to guarantee visibility for keyboard users in every context.

name: Reader
text: A 3px solid ring risks looking heavy on small touch targets—like buttons under 32px—where it may swallow the entire element. Instead, test a 2px #005fcc ring with a 1px #ffffff ring at 90% opacity; if it fails in Windows High Contrast Mode, the real fix is a 2px #005fcc ring with a 2px #ffffff outline at 100% opacity—only then compare against a 3px solid ring in user tests.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt the 2px solid #005fcc focus ring with 2px #fff outer stroke at 80% opacity for all interactive elements. Result: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance in high-contrast modes, mobile/touch visibility, and keyboard nav clarity. Owner: accessibility-w1.
